messages:
alex.w: Heads up — multiple training pods in us-west1 are stuck Pending waiting for GPUs but cluster-autoscaler isn't adding nodes. Seeing a bunch of pods with `0/1` Ready and nodeSelector: gpu=true. Anyone oncall?
ops-bot: Incident created for gpu-alloc-blocks (sev3). Paging #incidents-oncall.
oncall: I'm here. Can you paste `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide`?
maya: Pasted a filtered view:
```
# kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | egrep 'Pending|training-job-'
training-job-a-7f8d   Pending   0/1   0     10m   <none>   us-west1-pool-1   <none>
training-job-b-3c2a   Pending   0/1   0     9m    <none>   <none>            <none>
```
looks like one is bound to us-west1-pool-1 affinity, other has no node assigned. cluster-autoscaler shows no scale up activity in logs.
nate: Can you run `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,ALLOC:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu,ALLOCATABLE:.status.capacity.nvidia.com/gpu`? I think some nodes report 0 allocatable though they have GPUs.
maya: Ran it, output:
```
NAME                    ALLOC   ALLOCATABLE
us-west1-node-a         0       1
us-west1-node-b         0       1
us-west1-node-c         0       1
```
So capacity shows GPUs but allocatable is 0 on all nodes -> CA thinks they can't schedule GPU pods.
li: That screams device-plugin/kernel driver issue or kubelet marking devices as unhealthy. Check `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin --tail 50` and `kubectl describe node us-west1-node-a`.
maya: Describe shows this on node events:
```
Events:
  Warning  DevicePluginNotReady  7m (x12 over 9m)  kubelet  nvidia device plugin not reporting devices
```
nate: If device plugin isn't reporting, CA won't count GPUs as allocatable. Quick mitigation: restart the device plugin daemonset on the affected nodes, then uncordon/allow scheduling. We should avoid rebooting GPUs if possible.
alex.w: Can we patch without full restart? Maybe kill the plugin pods on those nodes so they respawn.
oncall: Good plan. Prepare commands and we'll run during a 1-2 minute maintenance window.
deploy-bot: Running command: `kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system` by oncall.
deploy-bot: rollout restarted successfully. Pods are terminating and recreating.
maya: New device-plugin logs show healthy registration: `Registered 1 GPU(s)` on each node. Allocatable flips to 1.
nate: Confirming CA logs now show scale activity: `scale_up: triggered for pending pods requiring nvidia.com/gpu` and new nodes provisioning.
maya: We did get one stuck orphaned allocation entry in the kubelet plugin: it left a device in 'allocated' state even though pod terminated. I force-deleted the stuck pod entry and restarted kubelet on node-b.
alex.w: After that, two new nodes came up and the pending pods were scheduled. Training jobs started pulling images.
li: Root cause appears to be a race in the device plugin with older NVIDIA drivers — when a preempt/evict happened it left allocations flagged. Filed follow-up: infra#342 - investigate driver/device-plugin handshake and add a health probe.
oncall: Good triage. Now decisions: 1) Short-term: add a CA webhook alert if allocatable GPUs == 0 for N nodes to prevent silent stalls. 2) Medium: upgrade device-plugin + drivers in us-west1 pool. 3) Postmortem within 48h.
alex.w: Agreed. Also add runbook note for 'if allocatable GPUs == 0 on all GPU nodes -> restart device-plugin DS -> if still 0, cordon + drain problematic nodes and force-delete orphaned allocations'.
nate: Cost note — restarting plugin doesn't incur extra capacity costs but if CA scales up because of stale allocs we may temporarily spin new nodes; keep an eye on preemptible quotas.
maya: Adding those action items to the incident ticket now. Closing here after I verify no more Pending pods in the next 10 minutes. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident gpu-alloc-blocks marked resolved (status: mitigated). Follow-up ticket infra#342 created.
alex.w: Thanks everyone, nice quick ops.
